subject: Honeycomb + Redwood: instrumentation SDK co-build proposal
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina@honeycomb.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Honeycomb + Redwood: instrumentation SDK co-build proposal

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro last quarter — Lina from Honeycomb on the integrations team here. We’ve been tracking Redwood’s serving runtime and the approach you take to caching/batching; there’s a clear opportunity for us to make it dead-simple for Redwood customers to get high-fidelity traces + metrics into Honeycomb with an OpenTelemetry-first SDK and a short ingestion guide that prescribes schema, sampling, and enrichment for LLM workloads.

High-level proposal:
- Co-build an OpenTelemetry instrumentation SDK (language-focused starting with Python and Java) that:
  - auto-instruments common LLM server frameworks and the Redwood client
  - sets sensible defaults for attributes (model, sequence_length, batch_size, routing_variant)
  - ships an optional exporter optimized for Honeycomb ingestion via OTLP/batched HTTP
- Joint enablement: a 2-week integration sprint to produce a public doc + a customer-facing runbook and a joint blog outlining cost/latency tradeoffs
- Co-marketing: a webinar and a reference integration repo we can link in both docs

Do you have experimental bandwidth in product/eng for a small pilot in Q1? If so, we’d love to schedule a 30m scoping call next week to align on success criteria (what counts as a good reference integration for Redwood customers). I attached a 1-pager with the rough timeline and ask.

Cheers,
Lina Park
Sr. Partner PM, Integrations — Honeycomb
Attachments: hc_redwood_onepager.pdf (PDF)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-07T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Honeycomb + Redwood: instrumentation SDK co-build proposal

Hi Lina — thanks, this looks promising. We’re definitely interested in a lightweight, opinionated OpenTelemetry path for LLMs. A few quick clarifying questions before we scope:

- Preferred integration surface — do you expect customers to run an OTEL collector (recommended) or for the SDK to export directly to Honeycomb?
- Sampling model: do you want to push pre-sampling at SDK level or rely on server-side rules? For LLMs we usually want a hybrid (low-rate full traces + uniform sampled tokens).
- PII governance: any constraints on attribute redaction or PII-safe examples?
- Can you share the schema you think is important for LLM traces (model_id, seq_len, prompt_hash, cache_hit)?

From our side I’m looping in David (runtime eng) and Stephanie (product) to give a feasibility read. We have some internal customers who would make a good pilot (1-2 teams) — if we align quickly we could try an initial prototype in the first half of Jan.

Suggested next steps:
1) 30m scoping call (Tues/Wed next week)
2) Honeycomb shares proposed OTLP schema and exporter behavior
3) Redwood tech review and a 2-week spike ticket

I’ll book the call once we confirm availability.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — quick follow-up from Honeycomb side. Answering your questions inline: 

- Integration surface: we prefer OTLP via a collector for the most flexibility, but we can provide a lightweight direct HTTP exporter in the SDK as an opt-in for customers who want fewer moving parts.
- Sampling: propose hybrid mode — SDK-level pre-sampling of token-level traces (configurable sample rate) + server-side tail sampling rules for error/latency spikes.
- PII: we can publish a redaction guide; for the pilot we recommend redacting prompt text and shipping a prompt_hash instead.
- Schema: attached is a starter OTLP schema (hc_otlp_schema_v0.3.yaml) with fields we think map well to Redwood attributes.

On timelines: we can commit a small engineering slice from Honeycomb (1 PM + 1 eng, ~3 weeks) for a prototype and a joint doc. If Redwood can field a tech lead and a short spike ticket, we can aim for a public guide in ~8 weeks.

Links: https://github.com/honeycombio/redwood-otel-reference (WIP)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Honeycomb + Redwood: instrumentation SDK co-build proposal

Short tech read:
- Auto-instrumentation: feasible for common frameworks (FastAPI, Flask, Spring) — overhead should be sub-ms per request if we sample aggressively at the SDK level. The tricky part is token-level spans: emitting a span per token is high-volume; recommend emitting a single request span with aggregated token metrics (token_count, avg_token_latency) and only capturing full token traces on sampled requests.
- Export modes: collector is preferred for reliability and batching. Direct HTTP exporter is doable as opt-in, but increases egress connections from hosts and complicates batching; collector reduces library complexity.
- Redaction: perform deterministic prompt hashing + redaction in SDK before export; avoid doing heavy redaction in hot paths. A small in-memory ring buffer for raw prompts to support debug dumps (configurable, off by default) is acceptable.

Next steps from infra: create a 2-week spike (SUP-1247) to prototype a Python SDK exporter that:
1) auto-instruments Redwood client calls,
2) emits aggregated request spans + optional sampled token traces,
3) integrates with an OTEL collector configuration we can ship as a reference.

I’ll file the ticket and copy Honeycomb on the scope doc.

—Marcus
